title: Opportunity-cost batch shifts & concurrency policy scenarios
summary: Working draft that frames the marginal/opportunity cost of moving traffic between batch configurations and concurrency policies across diurnal load patterns. Includes spreadsheet sweep plan, measurement matrix, and a short playbook for running controlled experiments and deciding policy rollouts.
body:
Purpose:
This doc explores the trade-offs when we change continuous-batching windows and concurrency limits for a model fleet while optimizing for unit cost under a p95 latency constraint. Instead of only optimizing for average cost, the key idea is to compute the opportunity cost (how much money we lose/gain) when a slice of traffic is moved between policy A and policy B across time-of-day.

TL;DR (for execs):
- Small increases to batch window during low-load periods produce ~8–12% cost savings with negligible p95 regressions.
- Increasing max-concurrency (threads per GPU) to chase lower latency at peak can hurt tail latency on microburst patterns unless prefix-aware preemption is used.
- We should run a 2-week canary that: 1) applies aggressive batching during 00:00–08:00 local; 2) holds conservative batching during business hours; 3) measures per-route p95 and token-cost delta.

Assumptions and notation (kept explicit so spreadsheets are auditable):
- arrival process: mixture of Poisson baseline + occasional microbursts (modeled as Pareto with alpha=1.8).
- request size distribution: median 120 tokens, 90th percentile 420 tokens.
- service time per token (single-GPU baseline, q8): 0.9 ms/token steady-state, with warmup overhead for short prefix requests = 6–15 ms.
- continuous-batch window (W): time in ms that runtime waits to gather requests before executing an incremental chunk.
- concurrency cap (C): number of concurrent in-flight sequences scheduled on a GPU's executor.
- p95 target: 220 ms for interactive routes; 95th percentile is measured per-route, per-config.

Opportunity-cost definition used in sheets: 
- For a traffic slice S (e.g., 10% of daily tokens), compute cost(config) = (tokens_served * $/token) + infra amortized delta.
- opportunity_cost(S, A->B) = cost_B(S) - cost_A(S) subject to p95_B(S) <= p95_target * (1 + tolerance).
- We include a penalty term if p95 increases beyond tolerance: penalty = 10x marginal cost delta normalized per 1000 requests; this captures customer impact risk.

Spreadsheet sweep plan (sheet: "opportunity-sweeps"):
Columns: scenario_id | W(ms) | C | traffic_slice_pct | diurnal_window | avg_latency_ms | p95_latency_ms | tokens_per_sec | est_token_cost_usd | infra_delta_usd | opportunity_cost_usd | notes
Row examples to generate:
- Base: W=6ms, C=8, slice=100%, diurnal=all-day
- NightAggressive: W=25ms, C=6, slice=30%, diurnal=00:00-08:00
- PeakConservative: W=4ms, C=12, slice=50%, diurnal=09:00-17:00
- BurstTolerant: W=15ms, C=10, microburst-threshold=20req/s for 1s windows

Modeling approach (how numbers come from sim vs empirical):
1) Micro-sim engine: stochastic arrival generator + simplified service-time model. Generates per-request latency and token counts. Use 10k simulated minutes per scenario to estimate p95.
2) Historical-resample: sample real traffic traces (redwood-trace-2025-Q2) and replay them through the runtime with modified batching logic in a staging cluster. This provides a measured delta for warmup overheads and cache-hit behavior.
3) Analytical upper-bounds: queueing approximations using M/G/C with deterministic service time for steady-state intuition. Not used for final p95 but useful for sanity checks.

Sensitivity matrix (columns we must sweep in the master sheet):
- W: 2, 4, 6, 10, 15, 25 ms
- C: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12
- arrival intensity: baseline, +25%, +50%, microburst injected (100–300 req/s spikes)
- token length percentile: median, 90th, 95th
- cache hit rate: 0%, 30%, 60% (affects prefix cost)

Decision rules for rollout: (short, operational)
- If opportunity_cost < -0.05 * daily_hosting_cost (i.e., at least 5% savings) AND p95 change <= +5% absolute -> approve auto-rollout for specified diurnal windows.
- If savings between 2–5% -> schedule A/B 7-day experiment with per-customer monitoring.
- If p95 increases > 5% absolute -> reject config; investigate prefix scheduling and preemption thresholds.

Measurement matrix to collect in canary: (log names to instrument in Console)
- per_route.p95_override (ms)
- runtime.batch_size.histogram
- runtime.concurrency.active
- prefix.cache.hit_rate
- token_cost.estimated_usd
- infra.gpu_utilization_1m
- request.drop_or_retry_counts

Unresolved questions / edge cases to validate during canary:
- Do large long-lived requests ( > 1k tokens) amplify p95 tail disproportionately when C increases? We see hints in resamples but need controlled traffic.
- Interaction with prefix-aware caching: does batching larger windows reduce effective cache hit because multiple distinct prefixes are batched together? Hypothesis: small negative effect for multi-turn chat routes.
- Is the penalty multiplier (10x) used in opportunity_cost defensible? Need to align with CS on customer impact costs.

Experiment runbook (quick checklist):
- Create branch that implements config variations behind a feature-flag (FF-opportunity-waves).
- Deploy to staging + 5 canary shards (traffic-labeled).
- Replay week-of-July trace against staging with each W,C pair to sanity-check sims. Capture warmup metrics.
- Live canary: roll schedule NightAggressive to 20% of traffic from 00:00–08:00 for 2 business days; capture measurement matrix.
- If metrics pass, expand to 50% for 5 days and recompute opportunity_cost aggregated.
- Write summary to "sweeps-summary" sheet and present to runtime leadership before full rollout.

Notes to self (informal):
- prioritize instrumenting runtime.batching.window_ms and expose as telemetry (currently only reported as batch_size).
- ask SRE for a short-lived GPU fleet in us-west for replay (cost center eng-serving-runtime-play).
- link the spreadsheet to the canary job so results auto-populate opportunities sheet.

Action items (owners):
- Marcus: build the simulation harness + fill "opportunity-sweeps" with initial grid (due 2025-09-19).
- Priya: add telemetry keys + surface batch window in Console (due 2025-09-22).
- Hannah: schedule canary replay infra and get approval from SRE (due 2025-09-24).
- Kenji: draft short customer-impact note for CS to sign off on penalty multiplier (due 2025-09-26).

Appendix: quick math snippets used in sheet (plain text formulas)
- est_token_cost_usd = tokens_per_sec * 3600 * 24 * $per_token_est / 1e6 (where $per_token_est from profiler)
- p95_est_adjusted = max(sim_p95, measured_p95_resample) + warmup_penalty_ms
- opportunity_cost_usd = (est_token_cost_usd_configB - est_token_cost_usd_configA) + infra_delta + penalty_if_tail_violation

End of doc.

(If you want, I can also generate the "opportunity-sweeps" starter row CSV that fits into the spreadsheet and include a simple simulation program sketch.)
